set-option -g status on

# =============================================================================
# Terminal & Key Compatibility
# =============================================================================

set -s default-terminal 'tmux-256color'
set -as terminal-features ",xterm-256color:RGB"

# Forward extended keys (CSI-u) so Ctrl+/, Shift+Enter etc. reach TUIs
set -s extended-keys always
if-shell 'tmux -V | grep -qE "tmux ([3-9]\.[5-9]|[3-9]\.[1-9][0-9]|[4-9]\.)"' \
  'set -s extended-keys-format csi-u'
set -as terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'

# OSC 52 clipboard (works over SSH)
set -g set-clipboard on

# Declare OSC 52 support explicitly for common outer terminals. tmux 3.2+ only
# emits OSC 52 when it believes the outer terminal supports it; most modern
# terminals (Ghostty, Alacritty, iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm) do. Without these
# hints tmux falls back to terminfo's `Ms` capability, which is absent from
# the `tmux-256color` entry shipped by many distros, so yanks from inner
# apps (e.g. Neovim over SSH) silently drop.
set -as terminal-features ",xterm*:clipboard"
set -as terminal-features ",ghostty*:clipboard"

I have a problem with <kbd>shift</kbd>+`letter` bindings in [foot](https://codeberg.org/dnkl/foot) terminal, for example default `prefix`+<kbd>C</kbd> (mapped to `customize-mode`) doesn't work. Following is my settings related to extended keys mode:

```
❯ tmux display -p '#{client_termtype}'
foot(1.18.1)
❯ tmux display -p '#{extended-keys}'
on
❯ tmux display -p '#{extended-keys-format}'
xterm
```
in my config:
```
set -as terminal-features 'foot*:extkeys'
```

Looks like `foot`+`tmux` combo report any shifted letter press as `S+letter`. If I explicitly do `bind-key S-C customize-mode` then pressing <kbd>shift</kbd>+<kbd>c</kbd> works as expected. In command prompt mode pressing shifted letters is ignored unless I press caps lock.

In editor like [kakoune](https://github.com/mawww/kakoune) which requests extended keys mode as far as I know, pressing shifted letter reported as `S+letter` instead of plain capital letter.

Following is what I get in extended mode while pressing <kbd>shift</kbd>+<kbd>c</kbd>:
```
❯ printf '\033[>4;1m'
❯ cat
^[[27;2;67~
```
Changing `extended-keys-format` to `csi-u` didn't help.

Is there any way to not emit `S+letter` in extended-keys mode without turning this mode off? Before update in tmux 3.4 there wasn't such an issue.
--

To troubleshoot further I display `pane_key_mode` before and after entering extended keys mode:
```
❯ tmux display -p '#{pane_key_mode}'
VT10x
❯ printf '\033[>4;1m'
❯ tmux display -p '#{pane_key_mode}'
Ext 1
❯ cat
^[[27;2;67~
```

Quote from the man page:
```
mode 1 which changes the sequence for only keys which lack an existing well-known representation;
or mode 2 which  changes  the  sequence  for  all  keys.
```

I suppose <kbd>shift</kbd>+<kbd>c</kbd> is falling into `existing well-known representation` category, therefore should be emitted as plain capital `C`. Please correct me if I'm wrong or if I should report to foot upstream instead.

CHANGES FROM 3.5 TO 3.5a

* Do not translate BSpace as Unicode with extended keys.

* Fix so that keys with Shift are represented correctly with extended keys.

* Revert to using /bin/sh for #() and run-shell and if-shell; the change to use
  default-shell only applies now to popups.

* Fix grey colour without a number suffix in styles.
 
CHANGES FROM 3.4 TO 3.5

* Revamp extended keys support to more closely match xterm and support mode 2
  as well as mode 1. This is a substantial change to key handling which changes
  tmux to always request mode 2 from parent terminal, changes to an unambiguous
  internal representation of keys, and adds an option (extended-keys-format) to
  control the format similar to the xterm(1) formatOtherKeys resource.

* Clear an overlay (popup or menu) when command prompt is entered.

* Add copy-mode -d flag to scroll a page down if in copy mode already (matching

I've checked and `set -g prefix None` allows to set a keybind that gets respected.

Additional notes:
- `client_prefix` boolean variable works (GOOD)
- `list-keys -N` stops working (BAD). in the previous situation (with default `prefix`) it would just show bad info on the first column for the `prefix` table keybinds, obviously because it does not know the correct prefix. Now, it just does not show any keybind in the `prefix` table (probably because a `None` value has to be printed). This is bad because as of today, `list-keys -N` is the only way to get the _notes_ associated with a keybind. I can still get those keybind with a separate call to `list-keys -N -T prefix`, but is is unexpected malfunction nontheless. A possible solution would be #2374. See also #4063. #2650 is also relevant because if `prefix` is set, and a keybind is set for the same key, `list-keys` would list the keybind but it will not work (because `prefix` intercepts is)

In summary:
- I can workaround my workflow with the proposed solution `set -g prefix None`, but:
- If `prefix` is set and a keybind collide, `list-keys` show the later but the former takes precedence.
- if `prefix` is `None`, `list-keys -N` does not know how to print it.
--

Thanks for working on this. Some initial comments:

- I don't see much point in supporting the xterm 27 form on output, most terminals and applications have converged on CSI u now. It is just adding complexity - I think it is OK to diverge from xterm here. It would be good to still accept it on input if possible, although I would be happy enough to discard that as well and just have tmux switch the outside terminal to CSI u by default.

- I think JUST_KEY is a bit pointless but if you must have it please make it KEYC_JUST_KEY.

- I think some of this should be broken off into separate PRs to make the diff smaller: utf8_fromwc, changes to KEYC_IS_UNICODE, and probably some other bits like the changes to the MODE_KEYS_* flags (even if some flags don't do anything to start with). You can do this at any point if you want to reduce the diff to master.

The code itself largely looks good, but as you say there is much to do. Most obviously is to get keys handled by tmux itself working.

There are also some missing pieces in the emulation if an application does not request extended keys - for example `C-1` sends nothing when it should send `1`, similarly `C-S-3`, `C-'`, there are probably others.

…

Do you mean simply dropping the `^[[27;m;n~` output form, so essentially eliminating the `switch` statement below, or do you mean more significant logic changes?

```c
switch (s->mode & EXTENDED_KEY_MODES) {
case MODE_KEYS_EXTENDED:
case MODE_KEYS_EXTENDED | MODE_KEYS_CSI_U:
case MODE_KEYS_EXTENDED_2:
case MODE_KEYS_EXTENDED_2 | MODE_KEYS_CSI_U:
	xsnprintf(tmp, sizeof tmp, "\033[27;%c;%llu~", modifier, key & KEYC_MASK_KEY);
	break;
case MODE_KEYS_CSI_U:
	xsnprintf(tmp, sizeof tmp, "\033[%llu;%cu", key & KEYC_MASK_KEY, modifier);
	break;
default:
	return (-1);
}
```

As for accepting it on input, I believe that's a must, just because of the robustness principle.

OK, just to make sure that I understand your proposal.

1. We don't react to `^[[>4;Xm` from clients at all, and don't send it out to the outside terminal either, essentially completely removing the support for `modifyOtherKeys` 1 and 2 modes,
2. We lose the ability to request the extended key reporting mode from the outside terminal, instead the user will have to enable the CSI u mode in their terminal settings,
4. If `extended-keys` configuration key is set, we output CSI u keys, otherwise VT10x keys.

In this case I believe we should drop support for `^[[27;m;n~` on input as well, due to differences in `Shift` modifier reporting compared to CSI u mode (and for which I still don't have an elegant solution in mind).

No, that's not what I meant. We request `modifyOtherKeys` as now. If the application inside tmux requests extended keys, we send `CSI u`. If they don't, we send standard keys. We never send the function 27 form.

- [keybindings.md](./keybindings.md) — all keybindings and the popup menu

- [vim.md](./vim.md) — tmux × Vim/Neovim notes and external resources

## First-time setup

After `chezmoi apply`, start tmux and run `prefix + I` once to let TPM install the plugins. The theme files also auto-clone their plugin on first source as a safety net, but TPM is the canonical installer.

## Version requirement: tmux >= 3.3

The popup menu at `prefix + Space` uses `display-menu -x R -y P`. On tmux 3.2a (shipped by Ubuntu 22.04 apt) the menu is positioned past the terminal's right edge and silently suppressed — the man page explicitly states _"If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."_ tmux 3.3 introduced position clamping and arithmetic in `-x`/`-y`, so the menu renders correctly.

The ansible `devtools` role now checks the tmux version and, when it is below 3.3, upgrades automatically:

1. **Linuxbrew present** → `brew install tmux` (latest stable).
2. **No Linuxbrew, x86_64 Linux** → download [`nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`](https://github.com/nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage), extract to `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/squashfs-root/` (no FUSE needed), and install a shim at `~/.local/bin/tmux` that exec's the bundled binary. `~/.local/bin` sits ahead of `/usr/bin` in PATH so the newer binary wins.
3. **No Linuxbrew, non-x86_64** (e.g. armv7l, aarch64 servers without brew) → ansible prints a warning; build from source or enable Linuxbrew.

### Switching a running server to the new binary

After an upgrade, existing tmux servers keep running the old binary (a live process doesn't re-exec on PATH change). Clients attaching to the same socket also stay on the old version. To switch over:

```bash
# lose current sessions but get a clean 3.3+ server
tmux kill-server
```

{"body":"### Issue description\n\nAs of a couple days ago—I think around the time I upgraded macOS?—tmux on my personal machine fails to recognize Control-Space as a prefix, despite nothing changing (as far as I know) in my `.tmux.conf` file:\n\n```\nunbind C-b\nset -g prefix C-Space\nbind Space send-prefix\n```\n\nControl-b likewise does not work, but sends `^B`.\n\nThis seems similar to https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues/4346, but mine is for the entire session.\n\nI've tried several things from killing/restarting the server to rebooting my machine, all to no avail. 短答：有風險，而且以你這個 repo 目前的配置，我不會把 `prefix + Space` 當 which-key 的唯一主入口。

我直接看了你現在的配置和環境：本機是 `tmux 3.6a`，而且你在 [common.conf](/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/common.conf:95) 開了 `extended-keys always`，在 [common.conf](/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/common.conf:97) 對 3.5+ 切到 `extended-keys-format csi-u`，主選單又綁在 [keybindings.conf](/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf:280)。這代表 `Space` 一旦送達不穩，整個 discovery UX 就一起受影響。要分清楚的是：你文件裡提到的 `tmux >= 3.3` 是為了修 `display-menu -x R -y P` 的定位/顯示問題，不是這次這種 key transport 問題，[tmux README](/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/tmux/README.md:45) 講的是前者。

Upstream 角度，`tmux` 官方只明確說 3.5 重做了 extended keys、3.5a 補了相關 bug；我沒找到官方寫「3.6 已修好 `prefix + Space` + `csi-u`」。相反地，在 3.5 討論裡 upstream 一度因 `C-Space`/`M-<` 問題把 `extended-keys` 預設改回 `off`，而且截至 2026-04-23 還有 `tmux 3.6a` 的 open issue：[`#4959`](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues/4959)（`C-Space ... send-prefix`）和 [`#4984`](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues/4984)（prefix rebinding semantics）。這不足以證明你截圖裡那個「bare Space 被 `csi-u` 編成 `CSI 32 u`」鏈條一定成立，但足夠說明 `Space`/prefix/extended-keys 這條路到 3.6a 也不能算穩。

純評估我會這樣選：
- 保留你現在的三層模型，方向是對的：[keybindings.md](/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md:111) 這個 `menu + fzf + cheatsheet` 組合比硬做 tmux 版 which-key 更實用。
- 把主入口從 `prefix + Space` 降級成 alias，改用一個 boring 但穩的鍵做 canonical menu，例如 `prefix + m`。
- 把 `prefix + ?` 當 canonical help/search，讓 `Space` 壞掉時還有自然的自救路徑。
- 不建議追求 Neovim 式真動態 which-key clone。tmux 的 `prefix` 是 special、key table 又受 terminal protocol 影響，做動態樹狀提示很脆。
- `M-Space` 只適合當備援，不適合當正式主入口。

一句話結論：`tmux 3.6a` 沒有給我足夠信心說 `prefix + Space` 在 `extended-keys always + csi-u` 下已經完全穩定；最好的方案不是放棄 which-key 體驗，而是保留你現在的三層發現模型，但把 `Space` 從主入口降級。

Sources: [tmux CHANGES](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/master/CHANGES), [tmux/tmux#4038](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/pull/4038), [tmux/tmux#4136](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues/4136), [tmux/tmux#4959](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues/4959), [tmux/tmux#4984](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues/4984), [tmux/tmux#4297](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues/4297).
